newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 12.

text.p: The president of leading plant construction company Chiyoda Corp, Masaaki Kashiwara, is expected to resign to take responsibility for the company's expected poor business performance in the year to March 31, 1997. Chiyoda is estimated to post a pre-tax loss of 17 billion yen -- its worst ever -- in 1996/97 compared with its initial forecast of 1.5 billion yen profit. The loss is attributed to lower profitability in overseas plant construction projects. Current vice president Masato Kitagawa is expected to become the new president.

Internet Initiative Japan Inc (IIJ), a leading provider of Internet services, plans to offer services for the development and maintenance of corporate Intranet networks in cooperation with Sun Microsystems Inc, Hewlett-Packard Japan Ltd and others. The companies plan to set up a joint venture this month. It will be capitalised at one billion yen, and owned 30 percent by IIJ, five percent each by Sun Microsystems and Hewlett Packard Japan, and the remainder by the other partners.

Sumitomo Metal Mining Co Ltd plans to join a leading Indonesian copper and gold mining project led by Sumitomo Corp and a U.S. mining company. Sumitomo Metal plans to provide several percent of the capital for the project. Sumitomo Corp and the U.S. mining company have decided to invest a total $1.5 billion in the project, and they hope to produce 245,000 tonnes of copper and enough copper ore to produce 16 tonnes of gold annually. They plan to start output from the latter half of 1999.

NEC Corp has started to procure high-definition liquid crystal displays (LCDs) from Hosiden Corp to meet rising demand for LCDs for notebook-type laptop computers. NEC has entrusted production of 11.3-inch high-definition thin-film transistor LCDs to Hoshiden. Hoshiden will supply the LCDs in semi-finished form to NEC's affiliate in Akita prefecture, northern Japan, for assembly. Toshiba Corp is also considering buying LCDs from a Korean electronics company.
